history.dynasty: Early Pandyas (original complex); later additions by Medieval Cholas, Pallavas, Cheras and the Madurai Nayaks
history.period: Sanctums and musical-pillared Mani Mandapam built by Nindraseer Nedumaran (Koon Pandiyan), 7th century CE; twin temples linked by the Sangili (chain) Mandapam in 1647; inscriptions from 950 CE onward
history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this CSV row (seq 2258, 'Nellaiappar-Kanthimathi Temple') is the SAME twin temple as seq 956 (id nellaiappar-gandhimathi-temple-tirunelveli, name 'Nellaiappar Temple', the primary record) - this file is the -duplicate record. The town itself is named for it: Tiru-Nel-Veli, 'the sacred paddy fence' - legend says paddy collected for worship was protected from floods by a fence of grain, and Shiva as Nellaiappar is 'the protector of the paddy'. A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung by Sambandar, it centres on two originally separate shrines - Nellaiappar and Kanthimathi - joined in 1647 by Thiru Vadamalaiappa Pillaiyan's Sangili Mandapam. Its signature marvel is the Mani Mandapam's musical pillars: two giant pillars carved from single stones, each with 48 sub-pillars that sound the sapta swaras (seven notes) when tapped, dated by the temple chronicle Thirukovil Varalaaru to the 7th-century reign of Nindraseer Nedumaran. It also houses the Tamra Sabha (copper hall of dance, one of Nataraja's five Pancha Sabhas), the 1000-pillared Somavara Mandapam and a Nellai Govindan (Vishnu) shrine. Stone inscriptions include those of Veerapandiyan (~950 CE), Rajendra I and Kulothunga Chola I. Administered by the HRCE Department. (The CSV's town 'Tirunelveli' is correct - no correction needed.)

name: Nellaiappar-Kanthimathi Temple
town_description: Tirunelveli is a 2000-year-old city in southern Tamil Nadu on the Thamirabarani river, once a subsidiary capital of the Pandyas. Known for its reed mats, palm crafts and the world-famous Iruttukadai halwa, its defining landmark is the twin Nellaiappar-Kanthimathi temple complex in Tirunelveli Town, about 2 km from Tirunelveli Junction railway station.

travel.airport: Tuticorin Airport is the nearest domestic airport (verify distance); Thiruvananthapuram International Airport is about 110 km per one source (verify).
travel.railway: Tirunelveli Junction (TEN), about 2 km from the temple; Tirunelveli Town is the older station nearby.
travel.road: 162, E Car St, Tirunelveli Town 627006; well connected by road to Madurai (~150 km), Nagercoil and Kanyakumari.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. The Aani Brahmotsavam car festival (June-July) is the grandest time - expect very heavy crowds.
